the find: *** A marriage declared unfindable, found by one phrase search. *** Nuestra Senora del Carmen La Mayor, Cordon, Montevideo, *** 28 DECEMBER 1871 ***. Image ark 3:1:3Q9M-C9B7-B3DF-C.
what the document says: *** "D. ALEJANDRO MAXIMO SERENA, soltero, natural de Montevideo, hijo de D. AVELINO y de Dona AMBROSIA TRAIBEL, con Dona ELISA VILLADEMOROS, del mismo estado y oriundez, HIJA DE LOS FINADOS D. PEDRO y Dona ANGELICA VILLADEMOROS." *** Two conciliar banns dispensed. Witnesses *** Dr D. JOAQUIN REQUENA *** and *** DONA AMBROSIA T. DE SERENA *** - the groom's own mother.
what it changes: Work-list row 185 had twice concluded this act "must be walked by image". *** IT WAS IN THE OTHER INDEX ALL ALONG. *** It gives his full name - the "M." is *** MAXIMO *** - and names his parents independently of the enrolment cards. *** AND ITS LAST CLAUSE PAYS FOR THE WHOLE SEARCH: *** Celedonia Villademoros is the daughter of Pedro Villademoros and Angelica Mendez, so *** ELISA AND CELEDONIA ARE SISTERS ***, a reading carried as "probably" since September. Both grooms are sons of Avelino Lerena Fernandez and Ambrosia Traibel. *** TWO LERENA BROTHERS MARRIED TWO VILLADEMOROS SISTERS ***, which makes the Lerena Villademoros cousins *** DOUBLE FIRST COUSINS *** - the same structure found at Trinidad the same day, a generation earlier and in another department. It also forces the 1873 godmother to be a THIRD sister, since the mother was already dead. *** WHAT IT DOES NOT GIVE IS HIS AGE ***, which is what the row wanted most, and that question stays open.

the find: *** The apex ancestor speaks, for the first time in this archive's life. *** Catedral Nuestra Senora de Guadalupe, Canelones - Religious Marriage Investigation Files 1776-1806, the expediente of Florentino Gomez. Images 340-341 of 457, DGS 008166573 item 8.
what the document says: *** "Florentino Gomez presento por testigo en esta Vicaria a SANCHO LLERENA, a quien se le recibio juramento ... el compareciente dijo: Que con motivo de haber andado el declarante EN LA LINEA DE VITORIA algunos anos, que conocio en aquel parage a Florentino Gonzalez ..." *** and, on the next frame, *** "... que dijo NO SABER ESCRIVIR, y la firmo su merced conmigo el presente Notario." ***
what it changes: Every other record of Sancho holds him as a father, a father of the bride, a spouse or an "other" - because the record index catalogues principals and parents and he was neither. *** HERE HE IS A SWORN WITNESS DEPOSING IN THE FIRST PERSON. *** This archive has held him since its first week and had never known anything about the man rather than his relationships. Now: a man who had spent years on a frontier line, who was trusted to swear to another man's freedom to marry, and *** WHO COULD NOT SIGN HIS OWN NAME ***. *** HIS AGE IS NOT ON THE ACT *** - the witness before him gives one, so the file states ages when it has them, and for Sancho it does not. *** WHAT "LA LINEA DE VITORIA" MEANS IS NOT ESTABLISHED AND IS NOT GUESSED: *** a "linea" in the Rio de la Plata is ordinarily a military frontier, and Vitoria is also a Basque city and a common Brazilian and Spanish place name. The open question on whether this family is Basque or Extremaduran is *** NOT *** advanced by it.

the find: *** A man of this name holding office, with a signature. *** Garcia, Clemente: Buenos Aires City - Probate Estate Case Files, *** 1800 ***. Image ark 3:1:3QHV-P3FJ-Z942, item 12 of 249 images.
what the document says: *** "Asi lo proveyo, y firmo Don RAMON LERENA, ALCALDE DE LA SANTA HERMANDAD DEL PARTIDO DEL ROSARIO, a seis dias del mes de Noviembre del ano mil ochocientos. RAMON LERENA." *** He notifies the widow *** DONA CELESTINA GONZALEZ *** and certifies *** "A FALTA DE ESCRIBANO PUBLICO NI REAL, POR NO HABERLO EN ESTA JURISDICCION." ***
what it changes: A rural magistrate of a district with *** no notary in it at all ***, which says something plain about how thinly governed that country was. *** AND HE WROTE: he signs twice *** - where Sancho Llerena, nine years earlier, could not. Two men of this family on either side of that line, and the archive now has both. *** AND THE PLACE IS NOW PROVED, BY THE COURT ITSELF. *** Hours after this row first read "indicated, not proved", the providencia that started the business was found at image 22 and it addresses *** "El Alcalde de la Santa Hermandad del PARTIDO DEL ROSARIO, EN LA OTRA BANDA ORIENTAL de este [Rio]" *** - so the Rosario is *** URUGUAYAN ***. And the widow is *** "Dona CELESTINA GONZALEZ, VECINA DEL COLLA" ***. *** THIS REGISTER HAS CALLED HIM "RAMON LERENA OF ROSARIO-COLLA" SINCE ITS EARLY WEEKS, ON THE STRENGTH OF A KINSHIP DIAGRAM DRAWN IN 1858. THE COURT PUTS HIM IN EXACTLY THAT PLACE, HOLDING OFFICE, IN 1800. *** *** WHAT HE WAS DOING: *** JOSE RIERA, Juez de Menores of Buenos Aires, ordered him to inventory the estate of DON CLEMENTE GARCIA because the widow was RESISTING it, having "pasado a segundas nupcias, teniendo hijo menor". Ramon notified her on 14 October 1800 *** in the presence of her second husband ***, began at "la nominada Villa del Rosario" on the 15th, decreed on 6 November, returned on the 11th with three men, and sat through the appraisal on the 12th. *** FIVE WEEKS OF ONE MAN'S WORK, RECOVERED FROM A FILE INDEXED UNDER ANOTHER FAMILY'S NAME. *** *** AN OBSERVATION THAT IS NOT AN ARGUMENT: the 1858 diagram puts RAMON LERENA and MARIA GONZALEZ at the apex, and the woman at the centre of this file is a GONZALEZ of the Colla. Gonzalez is among the commonest surnames in the Rio de la Plata and NO CONNECTION IS CLAIMED. ***

the find: *** A passenger-list name becomes a family, almost. *** Parroquia y Vicaria de San Jose de Flores, Buenos Aires - baptism *** No. 461 of 10 November 1912 ***. Image ark 3:1:939D-G6VB-K.
what the document says: *** "Bautizo solemnemente ... a JUANA, que nacio el dia veinte y cinco de Junio ... hija legitima de D. ELOY LERENA, natural de ESPANA, de veinte y seis anos de edad, y de Dona FELISA LERENA, natural de Espana, de veinte y un anos de edad." *** Godparents *** GREGORIO LERENA *** and *** ROSA DEFENARI ***.
what it changes: *** BOTH PARENTS ARE LERENAS *** - a fifth Lerena-married-a-Lerena couple here, and the first that is Spanish and urban rather than Uruguayan and rural, which is worth noticing before anyone explains the pattern by the smallness of a country parish. *** AND IT WAS NOT MERGED WITH THE PASSENGER LISTS, WHICH IS THE POINT. *** This archive holds a Felisa and a Gregorio Lerena who landed together off the INDIANA from Barcelona on 7 December 1911 and nothing else whatever about either. A Felisa and a Gregorio stand in this parish eleven months later. *** THE ARITHMETIC IS NOT CLEAN: *** the act makes Felisa twenty-one, so born about 1891, where the 1911 list says 1893 - and the archive's OTHER Felisa, who arrived in 1923, is recorded 1891 exactly. *** AND THE ROLES DO NOT LINE UP: *** the 1911 pair travelled TOGETHER, but here Gregorio is only the godfather and the husband is ELOY, who is on no passenger list held here.

the find: *** A null that got stronger, and a null the control EXPLAINED. *** Two of this archive's standing conclusions, re-tested in the second index on the same day.
what the document says: *** JOSE LORETO LERENA: *** "Loreto Lerena" returns three hits and not one is Uruguayan. The control was run *** AFTER *** the null - "Ambrosia Traibel" returns three pages including Montevideo parish records - so the instrument demonstrably reaches these registers. *** PABLO ARMANDO LERENA: *** returns ZERO. Control after: "Rosario de Santa Fe" returns 245 pages, so the corpus works and reaches *** ARGENTINA ***.
what it changes: *** THE FIRST NULL IS NOW MUCH STRONGER: *** it holds in two independent indexes, where before it held in one. *** THE SECOND IS NOT A NULL ABOUT THE RECORD AT ALL. *** The Argentine holdings the corpus surfaces are *** Buenos Aires probate, notarial and ship files - and there is NO SANTA FE COLLECTION IN IT ***. So the zero is about COVERAGE and says nothing whatever about whether the Rosario baptism exists. *** WITHOUT THE CONTROL IT COULD HAVE BEEN WRITTEN UP AS A THIRD INDEPENDENT CONFIRMATION THAT THE ACT IS NOT THERE *** - which is exactly the error this archive made in the other direction the same morning, arguing in public for a surname nobody had checked.
